title: store_soak_lane is flaky under parallel compile load - its planted-red check does not trip
evidence: crates/store/tests/soak.rs::store_soak_lane. api-int/A builder: failed once on write_p95_ms with concurrent cargo runs in flight, green alone. judge/A builder: failed with 'PLANTED RED FAILED: a deliberate latency injection did not trip a single criterion', green on a single re-run (10.27s vs 9.31s). Neither builder touched crates/store.
impact: a wall-clock-sensitive gate that goes red under load teaches every future builder to re-run and move on - which is exactly how a real red gets waved through. The planted-red self-check failing is the worse half: the lane cannot prove it still bites.
note: INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED BY TWO BUILDERS IN ONE RUN. Strong candidate for the next stabilize round: either make the lane load-insensitive (inject by fake clock rather than real latency) or mark it serial/ignored-by-default. MEASURED THIS RUN (8v8 plus earlier trials): base 1/13, merged 2/11 - identical rate and assertion, so NOT attributable to any landed card. Counted as an integration failure with no builder penalty.
measured: base 7a56d61: 1 of 13 runs failed. merged (wave 1+2): 2 of 11. Same assertion (PLANTED RED), same rate - sequential runs, same machine, never parallel. Confirms pre-existing, not a wave regression.
mechanism: drift_ratio is RELATIVE: bucket_p95[BUCKETS-1]/bucket_p95[BUCKETS/2]. The plant sleeps 20ms*(b-BUCKETS/2) for b>BUCKETS/2, leaving the denominator bucket clean. Under ambient noise the denominator rises enough that the ratio stops clearing the declared bound and the lane reports it cannot see its own plant. soak.rs:205-212 shows the authors already hit this and moved the injection once for the same reason.
